meta.datum: Elevations in metres above mean sea level (IGM / Genoa datum). Flood and river figures quoted 'at Ripetta' are gauge readings; the Ripetta zero lies c. 1 m asl but Aldrete and most historians treat readings as m asl, and so does this file.
meta.demWarning: The AWS terrarium tiles over Rome (z15) are a smoothed surface model, not bare earth: sampled against the INGV TINITALY 10 m DTM they read +8 to +25 m too high in built-up areas (Pantheon 29.7 vs 15.6, Piazza Navona 32.9 vs 15.4, Piazza del Popolo 28.2 vs 15.1, St Peter's 62.8 vs 33.0, Vittoriano 52.8 on the Arx), 10-30 m inside the Tiber channel (plane-tree canopy over the water) and up to 25 m too low on small steep features (Monte Testaccio peaks at c. 26 m instead of c. 49 m). Effective resolution is closer to 30-90 m than 5-7 m: cliffs, the Tarpeian Rock and the Velia cut are not resolved. Recommended: (1) use a bare-earth DTM (TINITALY 1.1, INGV, CC BY 4.0, 10 m, tile w46075_s10 covers the model area; it has its own triangulation artefacts in the dense centre) or (2) subtract each correction's dsmBias before applying its delta, and (3) let the absolute surfaces ('set', 'plane', valley levels) win over the DEM in the low city. Every valley point carries 'modern' (best bare-earth estimate), 'dsm' (terrarium sample) and 'tin' (TINITALY sample).
meta.hillsSchema: outline: slope-foot polygon (modern topography); summit: modern highest point (m asl); ancientTop: natural/ancient top; topLevels: optional time series of the top surface; subpeaks: named summits with modern 'elev' and 'elevAncient'; cliffs: lines along the cliff top with 'drop' (ancient, m) and 'dropModern'; 'artificial' marks built faces. partOf links sub-hills to their parent.
meta.valleysSchema: Points with absolute ancient ground level by year (linear interpolation between keyframes; hold the first value before and the last after). Use them as control points to build the ancient surface in the low city.

correctionsSchema.common: polygon + mode, applied for fromYear <= year <= toYear (inclusive). Where polygons overlap the higher 'priority' wins. dsmMean/tinMean/dsmBias = mean terrarium, mean TINITALY and their difference over the polygon (modern, m).
correctionsSchema.add: ancient = modernBareEarth + delta(year); delta from 'keyframes' [{y, delta}] (linear) or the constant 'delta'.
correctionsSchema.set: ancient = levels(year) [{y, elev}] absolute, ignoring the DEM (excavated areas, buried piazzas).
correctionsSchema.ramp: ancient varies linearly from elevStart to elevEnd along 'line' (projected position), optionally levelsStart/levelsEnd by year.
correctionsSchema.plane: ancient = plane through the three [lon, lat, elev] points in 'plane'.
correctionsSchema.planeMax: ancient = max(modernBareEarth, plane) (restores a slope that was cut away).
correctionsSchema.ridge: ancient = modernBareEarth + delta * f(distance from 'line') with f = cosine taper to 0 at halfWidth (and over endTaper at the ends); if 'crestElev' is given (absolute, one per line vertex) use ancient = max(modern, crestElev interpolated along the line minus the taper) instead.
correctionsSchema.mound: ancient = baseAncient + max(0, modern - baseModern) * scale(year) * (peakAncient - baseAncient) / (peakModern - baseModern); with scale 0 the mound is flattened to baseAncient. keyframes give the equivalent change at the peak.
correctionsSchema.sign: Negative deltas lower the modern ground (modern fill, mounds that are later); positive deltas restore ground removed in modern or ancient times (Velia 1932, the Trajanic saddle before 106).

meta.watersSchema: kind marsh|pond|stream|spring; polygon or line (streams have widthM, elevStart, elevEnd); from/to years; elev = ground/bed, waterElev = surface when known; 'becomes' names the drain or conduit that replaced a stream.
meta.certaintyTags: excavated | documented | reconstructed | conjectural (as in SCHEMA_CITY).

cliffs.name: Scalae Caci / Lupercal face over the Velabrum and Forum Boarium (SW corner of the Cermalus)

cliffs.name: North face over the Nova Via and Forum (Domus Tiberiana substructures)
cliffs.note: Here the face is mostly the brick substructure of the Domus Tiberiana and Caligula's extension toward the Forum (c. AD 37-41, then Domitian); natural slope before.

hills.modernDemProxy: good on the plateau; the 90 m-smoothed DSM rounds off the cliffs, which should be sharpened from the cliff lines

Heiken, Funiciello and De Rita, The Seven Hills of Rome: A Geological Tour of the Eternal City (2005)
Carandini (ed.), The Atlas of Ancient Rome (2017)
hills.note: Summit 51.2 m is Platner's figure. The natural crest is lower: the Palatine top carries 2-15 m of imperial fill and platforms (Del Monte et al.). Outline traced at the slope foot from the DSM and the known edges (Nova Via / Atrium Vestae on the N, Via di S. Gregorio on the E, the Circus north edge on the S, S. Anastasia and S. Teodoro on the W).

Summit 40 m is the pre-1932 garden level (c. 40 m high per it.wikipedia 'Velia (colle)'), the natural crest is reconstructed at c. 36 m.

cliffs.name: Tarpeian Rock (Saxum Tarpeium) on the S/SE face of the Capitolium above the Vicus Iugarius and the Forum

cliffs.name: SW face over the Forum Holitorium and Carmentalis gate (alternative Tarpeian site)

cliffs.name: N face of the Arx over the Campus Martius (now behind the Vittoriano and the Aracoeli stairs)

cliffs.name: E face over the Forum (Tabularium substructure, Clivus Capitolinus)
